objective: Add the proposed AOIC architecture specification to the current main baseline. This is documentation only and does not implement identity matching.
previous_knowledge_consumed: The current application preserves survey OIDs in observation contracts but does not provide a canonical cross-survey identity registry.
CatalogMatch and CatalogContext are contextual cross-match evidence, not a canonical object identity lifecycle.
DR24 OIDs must remain distinct from physical-source identity; OID grouping requires independent evidence and versioned rules.
The frozen v0.2.0 model, feature schema, class order, benchmark, and scientific acceptance criteria must remain unchanged.

baseline.description: Documentation-only architecture proposal; no runtime, schema, model, benchmark, or data changes.

correctness.before: No canonical object identity architecture document is registered on current main.
correctness.after: AOIC architecture and acceptance boundaries are documented in one versioned proposal.

reproducibility.reason: This documentation PR does not implement or execute identity matching.

scientific_validity.reason: No matching algorithm, catalog adapter, adjudicated sample, or scientific evaluation is implemented.

measurement.trade_off: The document defines proposed contracts and phases only. It intentionally does not create a database schema or production identity service.

evidence: CI must validate lifecycle record, formatting, tests, and package build.
CodeQL and Product Scope Audit must pass.
Review the architecture against current application and domain contracts.
Confirm the document does not claim AOIC is implemented or scientifically validated.
Confirm the frozen v0.2.0 baseline and CPVS research scope remain unchanged.

root_causes: Current application observation contracts use survey OIDs and do not provide stable canonical identities across catalogs.
Existing catalog context contracts do not represent an append-only identity decision lifecycle.

findings: Survey OIDs, catalog entries, detections, observations, physical sources, transient events, datasets, and analysis runs require distinct identities.
Coordinate proximity alone is insufficient to confirm identity; epoch, uncertainty, source context, and ambiguity must be represented.
AOIC must be additive and must not rewrite the frozen v0.2.0 benchmark or historical identifiers.

open_blockers: PR CI and documentation review must pass.
AOIC remains proposed until versioned contracts, persistence, matching tests, adapters, and independent adjudicated validation are implemented.

knowledge_carried_forward: Keep AOIC optional and additive until implementation feasibility and contracts are reviewed.
Use DR24 OID/filter/field/quadrant metadata as source identifiers, not as proof of physical identity.
Do not claim calibrated match probabilities without independent calibration evidence.
Keep AOIC runtime implementation separate from the immediate DR24 production observation adapter.
